plan: Trim SPY to 20% to cure concentration and reduce overall leverage. Trim QQQI to 10% and QQQ to 15% to rebalance broad index exposure. Sell SMH, SOXL, and SPAL to exit flagged positions and all leveraged ETFs. Trim CRWD to 10% to reduce single name concentration. Buy XLV at 15% to diversify into a strong sector setup.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with an expected ~1.5%/month return. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration, but still carries market risk.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure concentration. Trim QQQI to 10% and QQQ to 15% to rebalance broad index exposure. Trim SMH to 8% to reduce exposure to a flagged position. Add CRWD to 15% to increase exposure to an uptrending name. Trim SOXL to 2% and sell SPAL to reduce leveraged ETF exposure. Buy AAPU at 10% as a strong scanner setup.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech and new strong setups. Market fluctuations will still impact performance.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure concentration. Sell QQQI to focus on growth. Trim QQQ to 10% and SMH to 10% to rebalance. Add CRWD to 20% to press an uptrending name. Add SOXL to 10% and SPAL to 5% to increase leveraged ETF exposure. Buy AAPU at 15% as a strong scanner setup.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4%/month. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, leading to higher potential returns but also much larger drawdowns and daily decay. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Add SPY to 40% and QQQI to 30% to increase broad index and income exposure. Trim QQQ to 10% to rebalance. Sell SMH, CRWD, SOXL, and SPAL to exit high-beta and leveraged positions. Buy XLV at 15% to diversify into a stable sector.
income.read: This income plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions, targeting ~1%/month. It focuses on income and broad index ETFs, significantly reducing high-beta and leveraged exposure. While aiming for lower drawdown, NAV can still fall in market downturns, and distributions are variable.
